title: People
markdown:
**What it is:** Everyone OpenExecutive knows about, in two tabs. **Team** is the people who work with you. Each has a response SLA, a preferred channel and the approvals they hold. **Contacts** is everyone outside the team: clients, contractors, advisors, or anyone else you deal with. Contacts are private to you.

**What it does:**

- Add team members with their role, email, and their Slack, Discord and Telegram, picked by name.
- Set a response SLA so OpenExecutive knows when a reply is overdue.
- Assign **authority scopes** (e.g. approve spend under $10K, sign off on hiring) so proposals route to the right person.
- Mark the principal (you) and set availability windows or on-leave dates.
- Track **open loops**: what each person owes. You can assign someone a task with a due date, and overdue ones are followed up automatically.
- Show how each team member answers OpenExecutive's messages, and the writing rules it has learned for them.
- Keep **contacts** so OpenExecutive can email or invite them, only when you ask it to directly (in the web app, or from your own Slack or Discord). A contact can't sign in, can't message OpenExecutive, never approves anything, and is never chased.
- Keep contacts **private**: only you see them. Nobody else on your team sees the Contacts tab, finds a contact when they ask OpenExecutive, or sees an alert about one.

**Team member or contact?**

| | Team member | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| Signs in to OpenExecutive (with an email) | Yes | No |
| Messages OpenExecutive on Slack / Discord / Telegram | Yes | No |
| Approves proposals, gets check-ins and reminders | Yes | No |
| OpenExecutive emails or invites them | On any task | Only when you ask directly |
| Who sees them | Everyone on the team | Only you |

**How to use:**

1. Open **Company** in the sidebar (it opens on **People**). Pick the **Team** or **Contacts** tab and click **Add person** (or **Add contact**). Only you, the principal, see the Contacts tab. Each card shows the person's name, role, preferred channel and one status, such as on leave.
2. Choose **Team member** or **Contact** at the top of the panel. Enter **Full name** (the only required field), **Role** (for a contact, **Role and company**, e.g. *Head of Procurement, Acme*) and **Email**. If this is you, tick **This is me — Primary**. You can only set this when adding someone, and the principal is always on the team.
3. For a team member, expand **Contact & routing**: **Preferred channel** (**Where they last talked**, Slack, Discord, Telegram or Email; with **Where they last talked** OpenExecutive messages them in the chat app they last used with it, then any other app they have, then email), **Expected reply within *N* hours** (their SLA, default 24; items show as overdue on Home after that), and their **Slack**, **Discord** and **Telegram**. Those are also what lets this person talk to OpenExecutive on those channels. For a contact, they are under **Chat apps**.
   - Pick each one by name: type to search, then click the person. With an email typed, Slack shows **Found by email** with their name already picked; click **Not them?** to choose someone else.
   - **Discord** lists the members of the bot's servers. If it can't (the bot's Server Members intent is off in Discord's developer settings), enter their ID by hand.
   - **Telegram** lists people who have messaged the bot. Not listed? Ask them to send the bot any message.
   - **Enter an ID by hand** under each one takes a raw ID instead. A chat app with no bot set up shows only the ID field.
4. For a team member, expand **Approval authority** and click each scope they hold:

   | Button | They receive |
   |---|---|
   | Spend <$2K / <$10K / >$10K | Proposals for spend in that range |
   | Hiring | Proposals related to hiring decisions |
   | Vendors | Proposals for vendor contracts |
   | Credit | Proposals involving credit or debt |
   | Legal | Proposals with legal implications |
   | Board | Proposals before board communications |
   | Meetings | Meetings OpenExecutive wants to book |
   | All (wildcard) | Anything no one else is scoped for. Usually the principal |

5. Click **Add person** (or **Add contact**).

*A person's page*

Click a card to open the person. The page has up to four tabs:

- **Overview**: email, other addresses, how to reach them, and any leave date. Team members also show **Open loops** here.
- **Approvals & availability**: what they approve, and their **Availability windows** (days, start and end time, timezone). With no windows, they count as always available.
- **How they respond**: proactive messages sent to them over the last 30 days, and how many they answered. Kinds of message they reliably ignore are sent less often.
- **How I work with them**: how replies are written for them, learned from their own 👍/👎 and what they ask for in chats. Click **Edit rules** to type up to 8 rules, one per line; typed rules are always kept. The **⋯** menu has **Lock (stop learning)** / **Unlock (keep learning)** and **Reset what was learned**.

A contact's page has only **Overview**. An archived person has no **How they respond** or **How I work with them** tab.

*Change someone*

1. Click **Edit** at the top of their page. On **Overview** you can change the name, role, **Team member or contact**, email, **Other addresses** (one per line: mail from these reaches them and they can be emailed there; only the main email signs in), preferred channel and SLA. Slack, Discord and Telegram are under **Chat apps**, picked by name as when adding someone (it opens on its own when Slack finds them by email). **On leave until** is under **Advanced**.
2. To change approvals or availability, switch to **Approvals & availability** while editing: click scopes on or off, and use **Add window** / **Remove window**.
3. Click **Save**.
When your identity provider's directory is set up, a card marked **Directory** is someone it manages: their name and email follow it and are read-only here, and taking them out there suspends them here. A card marked **Link to directory** is someone already on People who is also in the directory: **Link to directory** in their **⋯** menu lets it manage them from its next run.
4. **Suspend person**, in the **⋯** menu next to **Edit**, switches them off without deleting anything: they can't sign in, message OpenExecutive, approve anything or be emailed, and their open loops wait. **Restore person** brings them back with their loops, working style and addresses as they were. Their card says **Suspended** (or **Suspended (directory)** when your identity provider's directory took them out). Only the principal sees suspended people, and the principal can't be suspended.
5. **Archive person**, in the same menu, takes them off routing and the active roster for good. They get no new assignments; their history is kept, but their working style is deleted and their open loops are closed. The principal can't be archived.

*Open loops*

- **Open loops** lists things a person committed to, was asked for in conversation, or was assigned. Overdue ones are followed up automatically. Click **Mark done** to close one.
- To assign a task, type it in **Assign a task** (up to 200 characters), optionally pick a **Due** date, and click **Assign**. The person is told once on their own channel, and the page says whether it reached them.

**Who can see and change it:**

- Only the principal can add, edit, suspend or archive people. Someone your identity provider's directory manages has their name and email shown read-only ("Managed in your identity provider"): change those there. Until someone is the principal, whoever sets up first can.
- Everyone signed in sees the team. Contacts stay yours alone.
- Anyone on the team can assign a task to anyone on the team. Only the principal and the person themselves see that person's open loops, **How they respond** and **How I work with them**, and only they can close a loop or change the working-style rules.

**Someone new wrote in:** when someone who isn't on People messages OpenExecutive, their messages are held and a card **Who is *name*?** appears on Home. Click **Add them** and choose **Add as a new person** (enter their name and pick team or contact) or **Someone already on the list**. Their waiting messages are answered once they're added. **Ignore** is in the card's **⋯** menu. Only the principal sees these cards.

**Example from chat:** *"Add Sarah Chen as our fractional CFO — sarah@acme.com — she approves spend under $10k and usually replies within 48 hours."* Or: *"Add Jordan Lee from Acme as a contact — jordan@acme.example — and send them the proposal."* Or open **Add person**, press **Ctrl/Cmd + .**, and describe the person. The help panel (the sparkle button at the top right) fills in the panel for you to check and save.

**Forward it to OpenExecutive:** forward an email from a client to OpenExecutive's address and it replies to you, not them, with a summary, a draft reply you can send, any dates or commitments, and an offer to add the sender as a contact. Mail a contact sends OpenExecutive directly is summarised for you, never answered on its own. Either way it stays between you and OpenExecutive: it tells no one else, and any alert it raises is yours alone.

**Just for yourself?** When you use OpenExecutive just for yourself, setup adds only you, marked as the principal, with authority over everything. **People** sits in the sidebar under **You** and opens on **Contacts**. Anyone you add from chat is a contact unless you say otherwise, and the **Team** tab shows just you. Other team members are hidden in this mode; the page says how many. If you add a team member (or move a contact onto the team), OpenExecutive asks **Switch to team mode?**: click **Switch to team mode** or **Keep it just for me**. Home doesn't show a People tile in this mode.

*Note: authority scopes are how OpenExecutive figures out who on the team to ask for any given approval.*
